dedupe_keys.name: kakhovka dam destruction 2023 water supply and irrigation loss in southern ukraine ceobs damage map entry

description: This entry in the CEOBS Ukraine damage map documents the Kakhovka Hydropower Plant at Nova Kakhovka in Kherson Oblast and its destruction during the war. It gives the context that the Kakhovka Dam and its reservoir provided drinking water to around a million people in southern Ukraine and irrigation water for about 400,000 hectares of arid cropland, and that the hydropower plant often balanced solar and wind generation. The dam was completed in 1956 as the last component of the Dnipro hydrotechnical system and had been modernised; after Crimea's 2014 annexation the North Crimean Canal supply was cut, and the canal had provided up to 80 percent of Crimea's water. The entry gives a timeline from Russian control of the dam on 24 February 2022 through to May 2023 and the destruction in June 2023. CEOBS is a UK charity that records environmental harm from conflict, and the entry has database ID 10177. Coverage: one facility and its downstream region, 2022 to 2024. Access: free web page; licence not stated. Caveats: it relies on open-source reporting and cannot verify damage independently. It supports cascading failure and water supply loss scenarios for infrastructure under attack, and relates to the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia irrigation record and the Kakhovka breach drainage model in the catalogue.
